name: Arjuna (Pārtha, Dhanaṃjaya)
summary: Kṛṣṇa's disciple and interlocutor in the Bhagavad Gītā. In chapters 13–15 he asks about prakṛti and puruṣa, the field and its knower, knowledge and the knowable (13.1, in editions with that verse) and about the marks, conduct and means of the one beyond the guṇas (14.21); he is addressed as Kaunteya, Bhārata, Bharatarṣabha, Mahābāhu, Anagha, Pāṇḍava and Kurunandana.

name: Kṛṣṇa (Vāsudeva)
summary: Speaker of the Bhagavad Gītā as the Blessed Lord (śrī bhagavān). In chapters 13–15 he teaches the field and its knower, the three guṇas and the highest person, and speaks of himself as the knower of the field in all fields (13.3), the seed-giving father of all forms (14.4), the foundation of brahman (14.27), the one seated in the heart of all and known by all the Vedas (15.15), and puruṣottama (15.18). Arjuna addresses him as Keśava (13.1) and Prabhu (14.21).
